question: A 65-year-old man with recurrent painless haematuria is found on cystoscopy to have a 2 cm high-grade, non-muscle-invasive (T1G3) transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder. After complete TURBT, what is the most appropriate adjuvant therapy to reduce recurrence and progression?

answers.text: Observation and repeat cystoscopy in six months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Observation alone is inadequate for high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (T1G3); intravesical treatment is required to reduce progression risk.

Correct. Intravesical BCG is the standard of care for high-grade (T1G3) non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer after complete TURBT — it reduces both recurrence and progression to muscle-invasive disease.
Radical cystectomy is reserved for muscle-invasive disease (T2+) or BCG-refractory high-grade NMIBC; it is not first-line after TURBT of T1G3 disease.
Radiotherapy is not standard for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer; it is an alternative to cystectomy in muscle-invasive disease only.

overallFeedback.feedback: T1G3 bladder cancer after TURBT requires intravesical BCG — it reduces recurrence and progression to muscle-invasive disease. Observation alone is insufficient.
Well done. High-grade NMIBC (T1G3): complete TURBT followed by intravesical BCG induction and maintenance is the standard pathway.
